Report the tools that a supplement site needs

Source: R/check-tools.R
check_tools.Rd

check_tools() looks for the programs and R packages that rendering and publishing a supplement site need, and prints one line for each. Run it before your first render, or when a render fails because a tool is missing. create_supplement() runs the same lookups after it makes a site and names the tools that are missing, too old, or not on the system path.

Usage

check_tools()

Value

A data frame with one row per tool and the character columns tool, status, and detail, invisibly. detail gives the path of a program that was found (with the version, for Quarto), the version of an R package that was found, or what a missing tool or an account is for and where to get it.

Details

The function looks for these tools, in this order:

  • Quarto: the Quarto command-line interface, which renders the site.

  • knitr and rmarkdown: the R packages that Quarto uses to run the R code in reports. They are looked for in the libraries of the R session that runs check_tools(). Quarto can run another R installation, with other libraries.

  • git: to commit the site and push it to GitHub.

  • gh: the GitHub command-line interface, for the gh release create command that release_supplement() prints.

It then lists two accounts that it cannot check:

  • GitHub account: hosts the site with GitHub Pages.

  • Zenodo account: archives each GitHub release with a DOI.

The function only looks for the tools. It runs none of them, and it reads the Quarto version from a file.

Statuses

Each row has one of these statuses:

  • found: the tool is installed. For Quarto, the copy is on the system path that R sees, and its version is 1.4.0 or later or unknown.

  • not on path: a copy of Quarto was found only in QUARTO_PATH or in an editor's folder, and its version is 1.4.0 or later or unknown. An older copy there is too old. The copy is not on the system path that R sees, so quarto render in a terminal can miss it. Add its bin folder to the system path, or install Quarto.

  • too old: the Quarto version is below 1.4.0, the minimum that the template's Quarto extension states.

  • missing: the tool was not found.

  • reminder: one of the two accounts.

Where Quarto is looked for

The function takes the first of these places that holds a file:

  1. The system path, as Sys.which() searches it.

  2. The file that the QUARTO_PATH environment variable names.

  3. The copy that RStudio or Positron installs, in this order:

    • macOS: /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/quarto/bin/quarto, then /Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/quarto/bin/quarto.

    • Windows: RStudio\resources\app\bin\quarto\bin\quarto.exe in the folder that PROGRAMFILES names, then Programs\Positron\resources\app\quarto\bin\quarto.exe in the folder that LOCALAPPDATA names, then Positron\resources\app\quarto\bin\quarto.exe in the folder that PROGRAMFILES names.

    • Linux: /usr/lib/rstudio/resources/app/bin/quarto/bin/quarto, then /usr/share/positron/resources/app/quarto/bin/quarto.

For the copy that it takes, the function follows a link to the file, then reads the version from share/version beside the copy's bin folder, where Quarto installs keep it. If that file is missing or holds no version number, the version is unknown, and the status stays found or not on path.

See also

check_supplement() to check a site before a release.

Examples

check_tools()
#> ✔ Quarto: found. /usr/local/bin/quarto, version 1.10.19
#> ✔ knitr: found. version 1.52
#> ✔ rmarkdown: found. version 2.32
#> ✔ git: found. /usr/bin/git
#> ✔ gh: found. /usr/bin/gh
#> ℹ GitHub account: reminder. A GitHub account hosts the site with GitHub Pages:
#>   https://github.com/signup
#> ℹ Zenodo account: reminder. A Zenodo account archives each GitHub release with
#>   a DOI. Link it to GitHub and turn on the repository before the first release:
#>   https://zenodo.org
